clue.text: Quarrel with son over expected performance on course

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
par is the score a good golfer is expected to make on a hole or course

explanation.surface: A golfer argues with their son about how they ought to be scoring on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the son on top of the golfing score.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to argue or exchange blows, a verb synonym for having a quarrel.

clue.text: Careless mistake students raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts its bottom to the top, so it reads upwards

blocks.note: pupils are school students

explanation.surface: Raising one's students' grades by error is a careless blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is an informal noun for an error made through inattention.

clue.text: Conclusions reached in weird case maybe alarm judge

indicators.note: conclusions are endings, so only the closing letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: the final letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A strange court case might well worry the judge presiding over it.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem is to consider or form an opinion of, a verb synonym for judge.

clue.text: Clubs are able to move up, showing spirit

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
can means are able
to go is to move

explanation.surface: Football clubs win promotion and celebrate in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'are able to move' turns round; the clubs stay in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, and brandy is a distilled spirit, so this is an example.

clue.text: Making rude observations about Tory leader in beginning

indicators.note: about means around, so one word surrounds the other here
'leader' keeps only the first letter of 'Tory'

blocks.note: staring at people is a rude way of observing them
the leader, or first letter, of Tory

explanation.surface: Someone opened by making insulting remarks about the Conservative leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting and beginning are synonymous present participles, as in a starting point.

clue.text: Was nothing ordered for president, initially?

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so those letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A question whether nothing was commanded on behalf of the president at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like a first-letters signal, but it is part of the definition: the first president.
explanation.definitionFit: George Washington was the first President of the United States, so the president at the very start.

clue.text: Exemplary kind of order for dessert

blocks.note: first meaning: perfect neatness
second meaning: a baked fruit pudding

explanation.surface: A diner places a perfect order for their pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase apple-pie order describes perfect tidiness, and apple pie is also a classic baked pudding.

clue.text: Star using Circle Line in capital

indicators.note: in places one group of letters inside another word

blocks.note: O is circle-shaped
L is an abbreviation for line
Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: A celebrity travels on London's Circle Line in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route, but here circle and line are split into separate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the Pole Star or North Star, is a named star in the constellation Ursa Minor.

clue.text: Some of you transgressed, quickly escaped on foot

indicators.note: some of means only a part, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: found spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Some of you broke the rules and then ran off quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrun pursuers is to escape by running faster, so the past tense means fled quickly on foot.

clue.text: Drive forward, as learner at end of parking line

indicators.note: at the end of places one piece after the rest

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a rope is a line, as on a ship
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A learner driver moves forward to the end of a line of parked cars.
explanation.definitionFit: To propel is to push or drive something onward, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Country like Norway, Sweden, or Denmark, in which child generally succeeds

definitions.text: Country like Norway, Sweden, or Denmark

blocks.clueFragment: Country like Norway, Sweden, or Denmark
blocks.note: first meaning: each of these nations has a king or queen as head of state
second meaning: a system where the ruler's offspring normally inherits the throne

explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeds' reads as doing well, as if the clue praises Scandinavian schools; it means taking over the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarchy is a state headed by a hereditary sovereign, where the crown usually passes from parent to child.

clue.text: Rugby forward, for certain, disrupted three-quarters, say

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so those letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rugby prop is sure to break up the opposing three-quarter line.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the three-quarters are backline players, which suits the surface; here it is the number 3/4.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator, and 3/4 is an example.

clue.text: Fabric okay for consumers, fit to be passed on

blocks.note: rep is a ribbed upholstery fabric
fit for those consuming it to eat

explanation.surface: Cloth suitable for shoppers that is good enough to hand down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumers' suggests shoppers, but here they are eaters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repeatable can be told again to someone else, as gossip or a story is passed on.

clue.text: Hooligan in area that driver tries to avoid

definitions.text: area that driver tries to avoid

blocks.note: first meaning: a violent lout, as a noun

blocks.clueFragment: area that driver tries to avoid
blocks.note: second meaning: the long grass beside a golf fairway

explanation.walkthrough: The driver is not a motorist but a golfer hitting off the tee with a driver club.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough is a thuggish person, and on a golf course the rough is the long grass off the fairway.

clue.text: Second prize in sight

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a pot is a trophy or a pool of winnings

explanation.surface: The runner-up trophy has come into view.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to catch sight of it, so the verb sight is a synonym.

clue.text: In alternative ways, met a person who's on one's side

indicators.note: two different ways of arranging the same short group of letters is wanted

blocks.note: these letters are used twice, rearranged a different way each time

explanation.surface: Someone met an ally in various ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'met a' are rearranged twice: first into a group of players, then into a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A team-mate is a fellow member of one's team, playing for the same side.

clue.text: One way to dismiss politician's platform

blocks.note: first meaning: in cricket, a wicketkeeper can ... a batsman out
second meaning: campaigning from the ..., a speaking platform

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman who steps out of the crease can be stumped, one of the ways of getting him out.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumping is a cricket dismissal, and the stump is the platform from which electoral speeches are made, as in on the stump.

clue.text: Drug's stolen recently, in attempt to secure next meal

blocks.note: pot is cannabis, plus the possessive S
hot goods are freshly stolen

explanation.surface: A thief's freshly stolen drugs are a way to pay for the next meal.
explanation.walkthrough: A pot shot was originally a shot taken just to get game for the pot, not for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A potshot was originally a shot at game to fill the cooking pot, hence a try at getting food.

clue.text: Became hard as rock, kind of

blocks.note: got means became, as in got angry
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Something set as solid as a stone, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard as rock' looks like one phrase; rock is actually the music genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Goth is a gloomy style of rock music that grew out of post-punk.

clue.text: Working with numbers, put in ten, as an eight is wrong

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of place and need putting right

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Doing arithmetic, someone writes ten because an eight would be mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Numbers' are not figures but things that numb; anaesthetics numb patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaesthetising means administering drugs that deaden feeling, so it is working with numbing agents.

clue.text: More than a dozen lines providing child with catch

blocks.note: a son is a male child
to net something is to catch it; 'with' simply adds it on

explanation.surface: A parent gives their child a fishing catch along with plenty of line.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a poem of fourteen lines, which is two more than twelve.

clue.text: Run fast, without a stitch

blocks.note: first meaning: to dash at speed
second meaning: to run naked in public

explanation.walkthrough: 'Without a stitch' sounds like a runner free of the side pain called a stitch; it means wearing no clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to move very quickly, and also to dash naked through a public place.

clue.text: What can be seen, in fact, as maniacal state of some Australians

indicators.note: what can be seen inside the following words is lying there visible, not to be built

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word, the whole second word, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Visible evidence that the place where some Australians live is a crazy one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is an island state of Australia, so it is where some Australians live.

clue.text: Part of deal, somehow — and ideal solution, moreover

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is wanted, so the letters lie inside them

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Somehow a portion of the deal is also the perfect answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The same four letters hide a second time in 'ideal solution', a bonus confirmation of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and moreover are both adverbs adding a further point, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Group of animals will, we hear, get over barrier

indicators.note: we hear signals that the sound of the spoken words matters, not their spelling

blocks.note: a herd is a group of animals, and 'll is the short form of will

explanation.surface: A herd of livestock is expected to jump the fence.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurdle is to jump over an obstacle, as athletes do in hurdle races.

clue.text: A number of Germans produced fiction

blocks.note: first meaning: a German art song, a musical number
second meaning: told untruths, past tense

explanation.walkthrough: 'A number of Germans' suggests several people; it is a single song, a number, from Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lied is a German Romantic song for voice and piano, and lied is also the past tense of tell falsehoods.

clue.text: Without external push, publish article that's cheerful

indicators.note: the word push split in two, sitting outside the rest, is to be removed from the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
the definite article

explanation.surface: Releasing a cheerful piece without any outside pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: Publish begins with PU and ends with SH, which together spell push around the outside; strip them away to leave the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means happy and carefree, an adjective synonym for cheerful.

clue.text: Odd statue I'd put in position

indicators.note: odd means strange, suggesting the letters are in an unusual arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone describes a peculiar statue they placed somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Situated means placed or located, a past-participle synonym for put in position.
